newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JULY 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JULY 18.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--Major Western firms will begin prospecting for oil in Greece at the beginning of August, 25 years after the discovery of the Prinos deposits in the northern Aegean. Interest this time is centred on western Greece and the Ionian Sea. The first contract will be signed next week with an international consortium including the participation of Britain's Enterprise Oil and the US's Union Texas.

--The winds of change are blowing ever stronger through the finance ministry with a recent proposal by the National Federation of Workers in Public Financial Services essentially supporting planned changes by the ministry in the tax scale. The proposals include the indexation of the tax scale by 20 percent, increasing to seven from the present five tax brackets with an increase in the tax-free threshold to two million drachmas.

--Deputy Development Minister Mihalis Chrysohoidis on Thursday referreed a truce between food producers and retailers. Both agreed to support the government's anti-inflationary efforts till the end of the year while Chrysohoidis undertook to draft a report by the end of August that will hopefully lead to talks to freeze prices at current levels for the next two years. --Domestic money markets appeared to be calming on Thursday with a lack of pressures at fixing and interest rates on a downward course.

--Conservative opposition party New Democracy on Thursday called for the government to develop and implement initiatives to cut back on public spending, bolster competitiveness and to contain state monopolies of public enterprises and organisations (DEKOs).

--The president of the Union of Coastal and Passenger Shipping Pantelis Sfinias said on Thursday that the development ministry's decision to set a ceiling on the retail price for bottled water and drinks on ships would not be implemented.

--International Finance Corporation will issue a 100 million dollar bond loan on the Greek and international markets in early August at Athibor rates, the first since the government imposed a 7.5 percent tax on bonds at the beginning of this year.

--National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou on Thursday was reported to have given strict orders to keep ministry and public spending to 1997 levels when drafting budgets for 1998. Most organisations have overestimated their spending to achieve the minimum. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
